title: How to Make an AI Music Video, Shot by Shot
summary: Learn how to make an AI music video shot by shot, from cast sheets to the final chase, with real prompts behind Catch Out, a residency short made in Flick.
body_markdown:
### How do you make an AI music video?


Plan the song as a chain of short parts, make a reference sheet for each character and an image of each place, then generate one shot per part with an AI video model and cut the shots to the song on a timeline. In Flick the song, the references and every take sit in one project.


### How many shots does an AI music video need?


Count them from your song: one shot for each place or action you want on screen, plus a few extra takes. Catch Out, a 4:06 residency short made in Flick, used 29 generated video clips, about 7 for every minute of film.


### How do you keep the same characters in every shot of an AI music video?


Make a turnaround sheet for each character, front and both profiles on a plain background, and cite it in every video prompt. When a character's look changes, such as a new haircut, make a second sheet and use it from that point on.


### Can I use my own song for an AI music video?


Yes. Upload the audio file to your Flick project, lay it on the timeline and cut the generated shots to it. Use a song you wrote or have the rights to.


### Can AI write the song for a music video too?


Yes. Text to Music in Flick writes an original track from a prompt with Eleven Music, where you describe the genre, the mood and the lyrics, on the Free plan.


### Can I make an AI music video for free?


You can start free: you get 100 credits when you sign up and 100 credits every week, which cover Text to Music and MiniMax H3 Max video. Seedance 2.0, which made most of Catch Out's shots, needs the Standard plan ($20 a month).


### Can characters speak in an AI music video?


Yes. Make the line with Text to Voice, then ask the video model to sync the character's lips to it. Catch Out's boxcar talk was generated with the words "Lip-synced to the audio" in its prompt.
